idea: Financial management consultancy for architecture practices
pain: Practices are run by designers who cannot model fees, utilisation or profitability
v1: A fee model and profitability review for one practice
verdict: Perfect credibility and a warm channel, aimed at the least solvent buyer in her whole network.

why.distribution: 50+ practices reachable directly; she is one of them and they will reply.
why.demand: The pain is acute and widely acknowledged in the profession, though budgets are thin.
why.fmf: An architect who became an equity analyst is the ideal person to fix practice economics.
why.defensibility: Her dual background is rare; the work itself is standard management consulting.
why.leverage: A reusable model and framework applied per practice.
why.tailwind: Flat; practice economics are structurally squeezed, which is the pain but also the payment problem.
why.ceiling: £6k x 33 practices = £198k, well beyond what this buyer segment will spend.

ceiling_arithmetic: £6k x 33 practices = £198k. Architecture practices are the price-sensitive, low-margin buyer the founder profile warns about; realistic conversion is 8-12 = £48-72k.
carries: The warmest channel she has and genuinely unmatched credibility with it.
kills: The buyer cannot pay. Every idea aimed at architecture practices hits the same wall.
test_fail: They ask for a favour or a payment plan.
